topic: Iterator Usage in C++ Standard Library Containers
explanation: In C++, iterators provide a uniform way to access and traverse elements within standard library containers such as vectors, lists, and maps. They abstract the underlying data structure, allowing code to iterate over container elements without depending on specific implementation details. Iterators can be incremented to move through the container, and comparison with end() iterators determines when traversal is complete. This approach enables generic programming and enhances code reusability, especially when combined with algorithms from the Standard Template Library (STL). Modern C++ emphasizes the use of iterators with range-based for loops and algorithms to write concise, efficient, and type-safe code.
keywords: C++ iterators, STL container traversal, begin() end(), generic programming C++
